summary: This note is a short biographical sketch of Alexey Brodovitch's early life. Born in 1898 in Ogolichi, Russian Empire (now Belarus), to a wealthy family, he grew up with a physician father and an amateur painter mother. The family moved to Moscow during the Russo-Japanese War, and Brodovitch was then sent to the Prince Tenisheff School in Saint Petersburg with plans to enter the Imperial Art Academy.
one_line: Biographical note on the early life of Alexey Brodovitch, born 1898 in Ogolichi and educated at the Prince Tenisheff School in Saint Petersburg.
key_facts: Alexey Brodovitch was born in Ogolichi, Russian Empire (now Belarus), in 1898.
Alexey Brodovitch was born to a wealthy family.
His father, Vyacheslav or Cheslau Brodovitch, was a respected physician, psychiatrist and huntsman.
His mother was an amateur painter.
During the Russo-Japanese War, the Brodovitch family moved to Moscow.
In Moscow, Vyacheslav or Cheslau Brodovitch worked in a hospital for Japanese prisoners.
Alexey Brodovitch was sent to study at the Prince Tenisheff School, a prestigious institution in Saint Petersburg.
Alexey Brodovitch was intended to eventually enroll in the Imperial Art Academy.
Alexey Brodovitch had no formal training in art during his childhood.
As a child, Alexey Brodovitch often sketched noble profiles of audience members at concerts in the city.
